message.content:
The answer depends on what you’re looking for—critical acclaim, box‑office success, or cultural impact—but if we look at the most universally praised films released in 2020, **“The Trial of the Chicago 7”** often comes out on top. | Film | Year | Why it’s considered the best | |------|------|------------------------------| | **The Trial of the Chicago 7** | 2020 | • Written and directed by Aaron Sorkin, it’s a sharp, fast‑paced courtroom drama that blends real historical events with a compelling narrative.
• It received an 88% rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a 92/100 on Metacritic, indicating strong critical consensus.
• The film earned multiple Oscar nominations (Best Picture, Best Original Screenplay, Best Supporting Actor for Ethan Hawke, etc.) and won the Golden Globe for Best Motion Picture – Drama. | | **Soul** | 2020 | • Pixar’s “Soul” was praised for its imaginative storytelling, beautiful animation, and philosophical depth.
• It won the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature and was nominated for Best Picture, a rare feat for an animated film. | | **Tenet** | 2020 | • Christopher Nolan’s action‑thriller was a commercial hit and showcased impressive visual effects and a complex narrative structure.
• While polarizing among critics, it still garnered a solid 78% on Rotten Tomatoes and a 73/100 on Metacritic. | | **The Invisible Man** | 2020 | • A modern take on the classic horror story, it was lauded for its suspenseful pacing and strong performances, especially by Elisabeth Moss.
• It earned a 93% rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a 77/100 on Metacritic. | ### Bottom line If you’re looking for a film that combined critical acclaim, award recognition, and cultural relevance, **“The Trial of the Chicago 7”** is widely regarded as the standout movie of 2020. If you prefer animation, “Soul” is the clear winner in that category.
